test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The current population of a town is 15,625. It increases by 8% and 12% in two successive years but decreases by 22% in the third, year. What is the population of the town at the end of the third year? ​
solution:
**Given:**

Current population of the town = 15,625

Population increases by 8% in the first year.

Population increases by 12% in the second year.

Population decreases by 22% in the third year.

**Formula Used:**

Population after increase or decrease = Initial population × (1 ± rate/100)

**Calculation:**

Population at the end of the first year = 15,625 × (1 + 8/100)

⇒ Population at the end of the first year = 15,625 × 1.08

⇒ Population at the end of the first year = 16,875

Population at the end of the second year = 16,875 × (1 + 12/100)

⇒ Population at the end of the second year = 16,875 × 1.12

⇒ Population at the end of the second year = 18,900

Population at the end of the third year = 18,900 × (1 - 22/100)

⇒ Population at the end of the third year = 18,900 × 0.78

⇒ Population at the end of the third year = 14,742

**The population of the town at the end of the third year is 14,742.**
